lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Running a GitLab workspace for twenty teams at once is a surprisingly good platform engineering job.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is that what Antoine does at Polytechnique Montréal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. He started as a teaching assistant, a chargé de travaux pratiques, on the DevSecOps course, LOG 8100. The CV lists the role from September 2024 to January 2026.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the work actually involve?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He built and maintained the course's GitLab workspace: repositories, CI/CD templates, runners and workflows for about twenty concurrent teams.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He coached Docker and Kubernetes sessions, where students build, deploy and debug, with lab scenarios guided by OWASP. He also refreshed the lab material, graded practicals and coached resubmissions.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why does he say it mattered?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because templates must be reusable, runners must survive deadline weeks, and every lab has to be reproducible on a student laptop. That's the same discipline he applies to his own CI/CD and homelab work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full post has the details and a photo from a guest session.
